== EXTRACTION RULES (GEMINI_HANDOFF_BRIEF §3 Task C & §5.2; CODEBOOK.md §§1-9; RISK_OF_BIAS.md §1) ==
1. ACCESSIBILITY GATE:
   - If `Retrieval status` is `not_accessible` (or the paper text below says `[FULL TEXT NOT ACCESSIBLE]`), you MUST set `paper_read = "not accessible"`, set `value = "cannot_tell"`, `where_found = "not accessible"`, and `comment = "full text not accessible"` for ALL 9 fields, and `evidence_quotes = []`. NEVER copy publication year or country from the citation header when the full paper was not read!
2. IF FULL TEXT IS READABLE:
   - Extract each of the 9 fields strictly from the paper text. Write a field value ONLY if the paper explicitly states it; if not stated in the paper, write `"not reported"` in `value` and explain in `comment`. Never guess or infer from context.
   - `publication_year`: 4-digit year printed on the paper/report itself (e.g. `"2024"`), or `"not reported"` if undated. Give exact page/header in `where_found`.
   - `country`: Country or countries studied as stated in the paper (use semicolon-separated names if multiple specific countries, or exact global/regional scope as stated, e.g. `"Global (48 countries)"`), or `"not reported"`.
   - `sample_size`: Exact sample size(s) AND explicit unit(s) of analysis stated in the paper (e.g. `"593 households across 4 neighbourhoods"`, `"128 municipalities; 2,048 observations (2010-2025)"`, `"32 semi-structured interviews"`), or `"not reported"` if pure doctrinal/legal analysis with no empirical sample.
   - `study_design`: Study design as the authors describe it and as operationalized in the methods section (be specific about quantitative/qualitative/quasi-experimental/experimental/review structure).
   - `effect_estimate`: Headline result of the study regarding how the legal, administrative, regulatory, institutional, tenure, tariff/subsidy, or participation factor relates to water/sanitation access/outcomes, with exact printed numbers (point estimates, units, 95% CIs, p-values, sample N) if quantitative, or concise factual headline finding if qualitative (noting `"Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported"` when purely qualitative), in your own words from the paper alone.
   - `risk_of_bias_tool`: Pick the single design-matched tool per `RISK_OF_BIAS.md` §1:
     * `"RoB 2 (parallel-trial variant)"` (individually randomized trial)
     * `"RoB 2 (cluster-randomized trials variant)"` (cluster-randomized trial — check unit of randomization carefully!)
     * `"ROBINS-I"` (non-randomized intervention / quasi-experimental study with a genuine comparator: DiD, IV, RDD, PSM, ITS, controlled before-after, policy panel FE)
     * `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies"` (quantitative cross-sectional survey / observational regression without quasi-experimental intervention comparator)
     * `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies"` (observational longitudinal cohort study without intervention framing)
     * `"CASP Qualitative Checklist"` (primary qualitative study: interviews, focus groups, ethnography, qualitative case study)
     * `"MMAT (Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool)"` (genuine mixed-methods study combining both qualitative and quantitative primary components)
     * `"AMSTAR 2"` (systematic review, meta-analysis, or scoping review with systematic search/screening; NEVER use for non-systematic narrative literature reviews)
     * `"Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework"` (legal-empirical, doctrinal-empirical, jurimetric, or institutional-historical study that fits none of the six conventional designs above)
     * `"NONE"` (fits none of the listed tools, e.g., pure mathematical/simulation optimization model, or non-systematic narrative review/essay without primary empirical data or systematic search — explain why in `comment`)
   - `mechanism_certainty`: Single integer `"0"`, `"1"`, `"2"`, `"3"`, or `"4"` strictly obeying `CODEBOOK.md` §9 and its design ceiling:
     * `"4"` ONLY for randomized trials (`RoB 2`)
     * `"3"` ONLY for `RoB 2` trials OR `ROBINS-I` studies with credible Low/Moderate overall risk of bias
     * All other designs (cross-sectional/JBI, cohort, qualitative/CASP, mixed-methods/MMAT, systematic review/AMSTAR 2, Legal Framework, NONE, or Serious/Critical ROBINS-I) CANNOT exceed `"2"`! (`"2"` = mechanism directly observed empirically; `"1"` = documented statistical/descriptive association; `"0"` = inferred only by authors).
   - `outcome_flags`: Comma-separated list using ONLY exact `CODEBOOK.md` §5 codes actually studied in the paper (`formal_connection`, `water_access`, `sanitation_access`, `service_coverage`, `service_reliability`, `service_quantity`, `service_quality`, `affordability`, `service_continuity`, `application_success`, `refusal`, `delay`), or `"not reported"`.
   - `mechanism_flags`: Comma-separated list of applicable top-level family codes (`ELIGIBILITY`, `BURDEN`, `DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION`, `ENFORCEMENT`) followed by exact detailed `CODEBOOK.md` §4 codes actually studied in the paper (`documentation`, `tenure`, `property`, `planning`, `zoning`, `building_permit`, `service_area`, `fees`, `procedural_steps`, `delay`, `discretion`, `hardship_exception`, `accommodation`, `administrative_review`, `complaint`, `judicial_review`, `disconnection`, `reconnection`, `sanction`, `participation`, `institutional_fragmentation`, `political_coordination`, `bureaucratic_assistance`), or `"not reported"`.
3. `where_found` AND `evidence_quotes`:
   - Every field's `where_found` must give exact PDF page(s), section, and/or table/figure number (e.g. `"PDF p. 4, Section 2.2; Table 1, PDF p. 7"`).
   - Provide 3 to 6 exact, contiguous verbatim substrings (`>= 25` chars, zero `...` ellipses, zero bracketed changes, zero paraphrasing) from `== SOURCE PAPER FULL TEXT ==` in `evidence_quotes` backing your extracted values.

evidence_quotes.quote: © 2023 Chumo, Kabaria, Elsey, Ozano, Phillips-Howard and Mberu. This is an open-access article distributed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY).

This study explored the co-creation process of iSAMs for WASH service delivery in childcare centers in two informal settlements in Nairobi, Kenya, and the self-evaluation of the process using FGDs and workshops.

evidence_quotes.page: PDF p. 5, Target population, sampling and sample size
evidence_quotes.quote: We sampled 100 participants comprising 34 childcare center owners catering to children under-5 years and 66 parents of children under-5 years attending the childcare centers in each of the two study sites.
In total 200 participants took part in our study, comprising childcare managers and parents (see Table 1) in the Methods section.
This was a qualitative study, using focus group discussions (FGDs) and stakeholder participatory workshops.

evidence_quotes.page: PDF p. 9, Step four: Learning and adapting informal social accountability mechanisms
evidence_quotes.quote: For parents who are not compliant with what we agreed, it is good to communicate with them, encourage and train them to pay in instalments for their children to access WASH facilities. However, when they cannot improve in their compliance, we do not allow them to bring their children to the centre

country.comment: Conducted in Korogocho and Viwandani informal settlements in Nairobi, Kenya.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, title and affiliations; PDF p. 4, Study setting; PDF p. 11, Discussion

effect_estimate.comment: Purely qualitative study documenting the co-creation and stakeholder self-evaluation of an informal social accountability mechanism process; no quantitative effect estimates or statistical tests are reported.
effect_estimate.value: Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported. Childcare center managers and parents co-created a four-step informal social accountability mechanism (iSAM) process to improve childcare WASH service delivery—(1) defining accountability to whom and for what, (2) performing actions and sharing information (fee payments and providing WASH amenities), (3) judging and assessing performance (via center visits, shared photos, and written/phone reports), and (4) learning and adapting (rewards, installment payment accommodations, or child exclusion sanctions for non-compliance)—which participants self-evaluated as enhancing mutual understanding, inclusion, ownership, contextual fit, and perceived WASH service delivery, while constrained by time burdens, leadership needs, inconsistent stakeholder commitment, and parents' financial inability to pay fees or purchase WASH supplies.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF p. 6, Table 2; PDF pp. 7–11, Results

mechanism_certainty.comment: Qualitative design ceiling is 2 under CODEBOOK.md §9. Rated 2 because the study directly documents through primary empirical accounts of childcare managers and parents how participatory co-creation, informal social accountability, fee obligations, installment accommodations, performance monitoring/reporting, and exclusion sanctions operate on WASH provision and access in informal-settlement childcare centers.

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines participatory co-creation of informal social accountability mechanisms between parents and childcare center managers (participation), parental WASH fee obligations and time/procedural burdens of multi-step co-creation (BURDEN, fees, procedural_steps), contextual tailoring and installment payment flexibility for non-compliant parents (DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION, accommodation), and monitoring/reporting with rewards or child exclusion for non-compliance (ENFORCEMENT, sanction).
mechanism_flags.value: BURDEN, DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION, ENFORCEMENT, participation, fees, procedural_steps, accommodation, sanction
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF p. 6, Table 2; PDF pp. 7–11, Results

outcome_flags.comment: Examines children's access to drinking/handwashing water and potty/toilet sanitation facilities in informal-settlement childcare centers, as well as affordability constraints among parents unable to pay center fees or buy WASH supplies.
outcome_flags.where_found: PDF pp. 7–9, Results (Steps one to five); PDF p. 11, Negative self-evaluation of the co-creation process

publication_year.comment: Published 12 January 2023 in Frontiers in Public Health (received 02 September 2022, accepted 22 December 2022).
publication_year.where_found: PDF p. 1, publication header, citation block, and copyright notice

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Primary qualitative study collecting and analyzing focus group discussion and participatory workshop data; appraised with the CASP Qualitative Checklist per RISK_OF_BIAS.md §1.
risk_of_bias_tool.where_found: PDF p. 3, Methods (Study design); PDF pp. 5–6, Data collection process and Data analysis

sample_size.comment: Total N = 200 purposively sampled participants (68 childcare center managers and 132 parents across Korogocho and Viwandani), engaged between December 2021 and May 2022 in 24 formative FGDs (8–10 participants per FGD; 8 parent FGDs and 4 manager FGDs per site) and 4 participatory workshops (~50 participants per workshop) followed by post-workshop reflection FGDs.
sample_size.value: 200 participants across 2 informal settlements (100 per settlement: 34 childcare center managers/owners and 66 parents of children under 5 years in Korogocho, and 34 childcare center managers/owners and 66 parents in Viwandani), participating in 24 formative focus group discussions (12 per site) and 4 participatory workshops (2 per site, ~50 participants each) with post-workshop reflection FGDs
sample_size.where_found: PDF p. 5, Target population, sampling and sample size, Table 1, and Data collection process; PDF p. 6, Results

study_design.comment: Primary qualitative and collaborative participatory study reported per COREQ criteria, combining formative FGDs, stakeholder co-creation workshops, and post-workshop reflection FGDs analyzed in NVivo 12 using framework analysis informed by Coleman's social capital framework.
study_design.value: Qualitative participatory study using focus group discussions (FGDs) and stakeholder participatory workshops with framework analysis
study_design.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF p. 3, Methods (Study design); PDF p. 6, Data analysis
